All green: `check.mjs` prints OK and all 18 tests pass.

Changed files:
- `bridge/acp-prompt.mjs` — new `extractBbContext(prompt)`: scans `<system_instructions>` blocks, keeps `Contents of … (project instructions / user's private global instructions)` sections, the `Rules the owner taught in this project` list, and `#/## Language` sections; drops plugin manuals, skills catalogues, memory index, reminders and preamble. Output ordered project → owner → language, capped at 16 000 chars with `…(truncated)`. `promptText` unchanged.
- `bridge/acp-tools.mjs` — `buildIntro` gains two rules: reply in the user's language unless project rules say otherwise; read AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md before changing files.
- `bin/muse-acp.mjs` — first message of a Muse chat sends intro + `Project and owner rules (from BB):` + extracted context + user text; later messages resend the context only when it changed (`session.lastBbContext`). `MUSE_ACP_DUMP_PROMPT=<file>` appends each sent message as `{ts, bytes, text}` JSONL and logs `sent <n> bytes` to stderr.
- `tests/acp-prompt.test.mjs` — marker keep/drop cases, budget ordering/truncation, empty-string cases, and a fake-mode end-to-end test proving the first message carries the rules after the intro, the second doesn't repeat them, and a changed context is resent.

APPROACH: Split each `<system_instructions>` block into sections at marker lines; bucket kept sections (project instructions → owner rules → language) and drop everything under plugin-manual/skills/memory markers plus preamble. The bridge prepends the kept context once per Muse chat and resends it only when it changes, so Muse follows project/owner rules without the ~184 KB noise.

LESSON: BB's system block is marker-delimited prose, not structured data — line-anchored markers (`Contents of`, `Rules the owner taught`, `# Language`, `The following … come from the BB plugin`) are the reliable seam between signal and manual noise.
